listings.name: Parc Maisonneuve and Jardin Botanique de Montreal
listings.content: The Jardin Botanique is one of the largest botanical gardens in the world and features the First Nations Garden, the Insectarium, the Tree House, and 16 different themed gardens and greenhouses.

listings.name: Parc du Mont-Royal
listings.content: North of avenue des Pins, between avenue du Parc and chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges. This beautiful, immense urban park tops the "mountain" (at 232, it's more like a hill) that overlooks all of Montreal and lends the city its name. Designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, creator of Central Park and Prospect Park in New York, the park is elegant and accessible, and has hundreds of nooks and crannies to explore. A broad and gradual 8-km (5-mile) bike and pedestrian path begins at the Monument Georges-Étienne Cartier (on Avenue du Parc, opposite the western end of rue Rachel, where the bike path continues), winding its way around the mountain and culminating at the Belvédère (lookout) and Chalet Mont-Royal, with incredible views of downtown, the St. Lawrence river, and the Eastern Townships. The Belevedere and Chalet are also accessible from downtown by the newly restored staircase, access via the path at the top of rue Peel. Many smaller paths and trails crisscross the park. For lazy visitors, or those with limited mobility, you can enjoy a wonderful view from the mountain by taking bus route 11, which stops at the lookout on Chemin Remembrance, and at Beaver Lake. Every Sunday during the summer, thousands of people get together at the monument on Avenue du Parc to enjoy the big tam-tam jam.

listings.name: Parc de l'Ile-de-la-Visitation
listings.content: Rue d'Iberville and boulevard Gouin, (metro Henri-Bourassa, Bus 69 east). This regional park is along the Rivière-des-Prairies. Quiet and enjoyable place to bring a lunch and relax for an afternoon. Good starting point for a cycling tour along the river.

listings.name: Just For Laughs Festival
listings.content: Comedy festival with three main components: indoor paid shows (usually stand-up, but not always), free street theatre/comedy, and a mini film festival called Comedia. July.

listings.name: Shakespeare-in-the-Park
listings.content: During the summer in parks around Montreal, Repercussion Theatre puts on outdoor performances of Shakespeare plays free of charge.

listings.name: Festival du Monde Arabe
listings.content: In November, an annual festival celebrating the music and culture of the Arab world takes place in Montreal. Many Arab performers, traditional and modern, take the stage.

listings.name: Festival Mondiale de la bière
listings.content: Annually, in June: several days of tasting beers, ciders, and other beverages from all over Quebec, Canada and further afield. The event typically offers over 500 different beverages, from over 70 brewers, from many countries. There is no admission fee, and samples typically sell for 2-8 tickets ($1 a ticket) for a 150-200 ml sample. There are also musical performances and food kiosks. The festival can get very busy at peak times (Friday and Saturday evening of the event), so it is advisable to arrive early to avoid possible long queues.

listings.name: Montréal en lumière
listings.content: A relatively new wintertime affair, attempting to transplant the city's festival magic to the cold season. Includes three main categories of activities: food and wine, performing arts, and free activities both indoor and outdoor. February.

listings.name: Montreal International Fireworks Competition
listings.content: In La Ronde amusement park (in Parc Jean-Drapeau). This fantastic festival features full-length fireworks displays, accompanied by orchestral music, by national teams from about a dozen countries around the world. Although the hot seats are inside the La Ronde theme park, the fireworks are visible from pretty much any clear space or rooftop in the centre of the city. Pedestrians can watch from Jacques Cartier Bridge, which is closed from 20:00 on fireworks nights. Another good spot is the promenade west of the Old Port. $35–45 (seats in La Ronde, free everywhere else). Saturdays 22:00 from mid-June to late July, and Wednesdays 22:00 from mid-July on.

listings.name: Fete de St-Jean-Baptiste
listings.content: June 24 is Quebec's national holiday (Fête nationale). During the evening, a huge show takes place at Maisonneuve park. This is the show to go to hear made-in-Quebec music. Free. Street parties can also be found all over the city.

listings.name: International Festival of Film on Art
listings.content: Devoted to the promotion and presentation of the finest productions on art and media art. A ten-day competitive festival, it is the most important annual event of its kind in the world. FIFA has become a focal point for artists and artisans from the art and film communities, and for art and cinema enthusiasts.

listings.name: Montreal International Jazz Festival
listings.content: The world's largest jazz festival, this festival is a major international event, attracting many big name artists. Many streets in downtown Montreal are closed off to traffic for two weeks and several concert stages are set up. There are many free outdoor shows and indoor concerts (paid). Late June - early July.

listings.name: POP Montréal International Music Festival
listings.content: A massive feast of up-and-coming bands in a variety of popular genres. In early fall, host to more than 80 events, more than 300 artists, a conference, and an arts fair. POP Montreal showcases emerging and innovative artists alongside rising international stars and is committed to encouraging vibrant indie communities.

listings.name: Francofolies
listings.content: A festival celebrating French-language music from around the world. Similarly to the jazz festival, many free outdoor concerts are offered in a section of downtown that is closed off to traffic for a week. Mid-June.

listings.name: MUTEK
listings.content: An annual gathering, held in Montreal. The MUTEK festival showcases emerging forms of electronic music and the latest trends in sound creation.

listings.name: Heavy Montréal
listings.content: A two-day heavy music festival taking place in Parc Jean-Drapeau on Île Sainte-Hélène.

listings.name: Osheaga Music and Arts Festival
listings.content: A three-day indie & alternative rock festival held annually in Parc Jean-Drapeau on Île Sainte-Hélène at the end of July/beginning of August.

listings.name: Fantasia
listings.content: July.

listings.name: Image + Nation
listings.content: November/December.

listings.name: Festival du nouveau cinéma de Montréal
listings.content: October.

listings.name: Cinémania
listings.content: November.

listings.name: Les Rencontres internationales du documentaire de Montréal
listings.content: November.

listings.name: Les Rendez-vous du cinéma québécois
listings.content: February.

listings.name: Brasserie La Cage
listings.content: Sports bar and grill. Great place to watch Montreal Canadiens hockey games, the atmosphere gets crazy during the NHL playoffs!

listings.name: Les Trois Brasseurs
listings.content: Microbrewery with a pub-style menu and a European flair.

listings.name: Juliette et chocolat
listings.content: Specialised in chocolate desserts and famed for its very rich drinking chocolate.

listings.name: Rockaberry
listings.content: Enormous portions of cakes, pies, crumbles and brownies.

listings.name: Copper Branch
listings.content: Vegan chain serving sandwiches, wraps, soups and some desserts.

listings.name: St. Joseph's Oratory
listings.content: The largest church in Canada, it has an impressive neo-Renaissance exterior and a contemporary bell tower. The Basilica has a beautiful, restrained, somewhat stark Art Deco interior, complete with unusual, elongated wooden statues of saints, and combined with the great height of its ceiling, it may seem somewhat forbidding, but it also has a more traditionally expressive series of statues of the Stations of the Cross and Crucifix at the altar and a pretty series of mosaics behind the altar. It is a favourite pilgrimage for devotees of Brother André, who was reputed to have healed the sick and handicapped. Includes a remarkable collection of crutches and canes from the healed. In good weather, it is also possible to stroll through the beautiful garden next to the Oratory which features the Stations of the Cross in marble sculptures. The garden is peaceful and beautifully maintained. The views from both the Oratory and the garden are magnificent and well-worth the climb. Watch for the faithful climbing on their knees to the top.

listings.name: Notre-Dame-des-Neiges Cemetery
listings.content: One of the largest cemeteries in Canada.

listings.name: Université de Montréal
listings.content: The second largest university in Canada in terms of students, Université de Montréal is a French speaking university whose campus is mostly concentrated on the mount Royal, between the metro stations Edouard-Montpetit and Côte-des-Neiges. The Roger-Gaudry building, with its tall tower and Art Deco architecture, is well worth a look. It is just in front of the metro station Université-de-Montréal.

listings.name: The Montreal Holocaust Memorial Centre
listings.content: Dedicated to Holocaust education and awareness. It was founded in 1979 by a group of Holocaust survivors. The Centre's mandate is to educate people of all ages and backgrounds about the genocidal murder of six million Jews by Nazi Germany and its collaborators between 1933-1945.
listings.address: 1 Carré Cummings Square (5151 Chemin de la Côte-Sainte–Catherine)

listings.name: The Segal Centre for Performing Arts
Piscine Cote-des-Neiges
listings.content: Indoor swimming pool.

listings.name: Picnic in the park
listings.content: Relax in the park with your lunch. There are several grocery stores nearby, and many restaurants that offer take out (mostly on Gatineau and Côte-des-Neiges).

listings.name: Chez Benny
listings.content: Kosher restaurant with Mediterranean (shawarma, falafel, merguez and the likes) and Chinese dishes. Really busy on weekend evenings.

listings.name: Ernie's and Ellie's Place
listings.content: Kosher meat restaurant. Everything goes: Russian, Chinese, Moroccan, you name it. Regular "Canadian" kitchen isn't bad either. Food served very quickly. Decor is trying to be nice but misses some edge. It doesn't matter though, because this place gets customers no matter what happens.

listings.name: Expresti gourmet
listings.content: Italian, dairy and Parve.

listings.name: Pizza Pita
listings.content: Kosher (and Cholov Yisroel) pizzas, pita sandwiches, burgers. Falafels are generously stuffed and fried eggplants give a tasty twist. Very popular with high schoolers and the frum set, especially on Saturday nights. One of the best veggie pizzas in Montreal.

listings.name: Pizzeria Tatty
listings.content: Kosher pizzeria.

listings.name: The Reserve
listings.content: Kosher steakhouse and tavern.

listings.name: Exception 2
listings.content: Kosher dairy restaurant featuring thin crust pizzas.

listings.name: Chez Jolee
listings.content: Delicious Sri Lankan and South Indian meals and snacks, including dosa, kottu roti, string hoppers, idli, vada and more.

listings.name: Al Amine
listings.content: Typical Montreal-style "shish taouk" (chicken shawarma) Lebanese restaurant. Delicious and rather healthy fast food. They have great vegetarian/vegan options (falafel, vegetarian platter), pizza by the slice and Lebanese baklava.

listings.name: Le Camélia des tropiques
listings.content: Unusually good (for Montreal) Vietnamese food. Phõ, meats, seafood, and veggie curries. Ask for the "by-request" extra hot hot sauce.

listings.name: Restaurant Mavi
listings.content: Authentic Portuguese restaurant, famous for its charcoal grilled chicken. The fries are killer too! Eat your lunch at the restaurant or take it to go and picnic in the park on the other side of the street.

listings.name: La Saigonnaise
listings.content: Fantastic Thai and Vietnamese restaurant. Share a "volcanic island" with friends or enjoy your own table d'hôte.

listings.name: Il Galateo
listings.content: You could easily walk by without noticing this subterranean Italian restaurant, but you'd be missing out on a secret gem. Standard pasta, meat, and seafood plus a few surprises like dandelion salad.

listings.name: Tabasco Bar
listings.content: Restaurant and club. Also has a pool table. The food is pretty average.

listings.name: La Maisonnée
listings.content: Also serves food, very popular amongst university students. Karaoke on certain nights.

listings.name: McCarold's
listings.content: Great Irish pub, also serves very good food, try the burgers (they have an exquisite vegetarian burger too). This pub has the best selection of beers in the neighborhood, with the usual pub beers (Guinness, Kilkenny), good local beers on tap (from Unibroue and Boréale) and an impressive selection of international (UK, Belgium) and local microbrew bottled beer. They also have hard cider, whisky and cocktails.

listings.name: Studio Hotel
listings.content: Open May to 29 Aug, Studio Hotel offers 800 budget rooms next to University of Montreal. Modern, clean, shared kitchen, common rooms, and gym.
listings.price: starting at $40/night for single studio up to $100 for suite

listings.name: McGill University Campus
listings.content: The lower section of McGill's campus is composed mainly of 19th-century neoclassical buildings and is definitely worth a ten-minute stroll.
listings.address: 805 rue Sherbrooke ouest at ave McGill College

listings.name: The Underground City
listings.content: Throughout the downtown area. This network of underground malls and passageways is a very convenient way to walk around during the winter months. It encompasses six metro stations on the green and orange lines and all of the major downtown shopping malls, including food courts, cinemas, innumerable boutiques, and services.

listings.name: Christ Church Cathedral
listings.content: It is a small, but colourful church, the mother church of the region's Anglican (Episcopalian) denomination. Of special interest is the organ with additional remote-controlled organ pipes in the front of the church. If you have the opportunity to listen to an organ concert there, you should go. The concert will probably be by donation only.

listings.name: Mary Queen of the World Cathedral
listings.content: A 1/4 scale copy of St. Peter's in Rome. Impressive interior.

listings.name: Canadian Centre for Architecture
listings.content: Architecture museum and research institute that incorporates the Shaughnessy House, an 1876 Second Empire-style manison. Across boulevard René-Lévesque from the CCA is a sculpture garden with works designed around the theme of architecture. Guided tours available.
listings.price: $10 adults, $7 seniors, free for students and children

listings.name: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts
listings.content: Many prominent travelling exhibits.

listings.name: McCord Museum
listings.content: Museum dedicated to Canadian history, next to McGill University.

listings.name: Musée d'art contemporain de Montréal
listings.content: Contemporary art museum at the Place-des-Arts complex.
listings.price: $15 adult, $12 senior (60+), $10 students (18+ with ID), free for children (0-12), $5 youth (13-17), $30 family, children free

listings.name: Redpath Museum
listings.content: A museum of natural history on the McGill campus.

listings.name: Windsor Station
listings.content: This Romanesque Revival building served as one of the city's main railway stations until it was cut off from the rail network by the construction of the Bell Centre nearby.
listings.image: Estación de Windsor, Montreal, Canadá, 2017-08-11, DD 35.jpg

listings.name: Habitat 67
listings.content: This visually striking residential building was created by architect Moshe Safdie for Expo 67. The result was an amazingly modern dwelling that challenged the way architects created urban homes. Compared alternately to a beehive, a Taos pueblo, and a crystalline growth, the complex's 154 units are composed of prefabricated concrete cubes assembled on site. The apartments here are highly prized and a number of prominent Montrealers make Habitat 67 their home.

listings.name: Place Sun-Yat-Sen
listings.content: A small public square in the middle of Chinatown. There are murals made of grey slate along the north and east side of the square; also at the square is a pavilion selling typical Chinatown tourist souvenirs.
listings.address: rue de la Gauchetière and rue Clark

listings.name: Chalet du Mont-Royal
listings.content: Built as a make-work project in 1932 during the Great Depression. The interior features artwork depicting various scenes from Canadian history.
listings.address: up the stairs from Redpath Crescent

listings.name: Kondiaronk Lookout
listings.content: Offers panoramic views of the downtown Montreal skyline.
listings.address: next to the Chalet du Mont-Royal

listings.name: Croix du Mont-Royal
listings.content: A white illuminated cross installed in 1924 at the site where Paul Chomedey de Maisonneuve planted a wooden cross in 1643. He allegedly planted it there after praying to the Virgin Mary to spare the city of Montreal from a flood.

listings.name: Lac des Castors
listings.content: Man-made lake in a former marsh. Paddleboats are rented out in summer; in winter the lake becomes an ice skating rink.

listings.name: Monument à George-Étienne Cartier
listings.content: A 1919 monument sculpted by George William Hill in honor of Georges-Étienne Cartier, one of the fathers of Confederation.
listings.address: along chemin Olmsted on the east side of Parc du Mont-Royal

listings.name: Belvédère Camillien-Houde
listings.content: Another lookout point.
listings.address: voie Camillien-Houde across from Cimetière Mont-Royal

listings.name: Maison Smith
listings.address: near Chemin Remembrance and voie Camillien-Houde

listings.name: Bell Centre
listings.content: Home of the Montreal Canadiens ice hockey team, commonly known as the Habs. Also hosts larger concerts.

listings.name: Molson Stadium
listings.content: An outdoor Canadian football stadium on the McGill campus. The McGill Redbirds (Quebec University Football League) and the Montreal Alouettes (Canadian Football League) play here.

listings.name: Montreal Forum / Pepsi Forum
listings.content: An entertainment complex at the site of the former home of the Canadiens from 1926-1996. It is home to an AMC Cinema (22 screens) and The Montreal Comedy Nest.

listings.name: Café Presto
listings.content: The best downtown deal for a very inexpensive and very satisfying casual/cozy Italian fare (main courses are all $5.95. Calculate approximately $20 if you add a glass of wine and an espresso). Very busy during lunchtime on weekdays. Arrive before noon or after 13:30 to avoid the longest lines. Cash only (no credit or debit cards, but there are a few ATMs on the same block).

listings.name: Café Crystal
listings.content: Light meals for breakfast and lunch. $5-7, close to the rue Sainte-Catherine shopping district.

listings.name: Cafe Dizengoff
listings.content: Kosher cafe on the ground floor of the Hillel House, on the McGill campus.

listings.name: Dunn's Famous
listings.content: Opened in 1927. It has smoked meat and poutine dishes.

listings.name: Il Focolaio
listings.content: Delicious pizza, wine and tiramisu.

listings.name: SAT
listings.content: This one-of-a-kind venue is supported by the province of Quebec and the federal government to display and promote digital art. With high ceilings and low couches, it has the feel of a funky, uber-hip techno club. In fact, there is quite a bit of great club music on weekend nights. But there's also fascinating computer art installations going on at all times, with some video and live performances. A great place to meet people in Montreal.

listings.name: Bar des Pins
listings.content: Blue-collar bar invaded regularly by beer-pong-playing university students. Sells only cheap beer. Hottest night of the week is Tuesday.

listings.name: Vinyl
listings.content: Vinyl is a small, intimate club with frequent specials including $3 Rhum-n-Tings on Sunday nights and a diverse range of music from Reggae to Techno on different nights. Also, couches in the bathroom and an outdoor terrace around the back.

listings.name: The Cock n' Bull
listings.content: Inexpensive pub with a small kitchen, live bands, a single pool table and a couple of active dart boards. Known for their cheap 4 Liters beer pitchers (16 $). Friendly and sociable, for the most part English-speaking patrons, from age 18 to 60. Arts and crafts on Monday nights!

listings.name: McKibbin's Irish Pub
listings.content: Being next door to Concordia University may or may not be a point in its favor, but there's no denying that this friendly pub is a great place for a pint. The food is above-average for a pub, too. McKibbin's is known for their ladies night every Wednesday with its all night open bar ($10 cover for girls and $25 cover for guys).

listings.name: Hurley's
listings.content: Probably the best Irish pub in Montreal, with live traditional music every night and excellent food at fair prices. There's an upstairs for the busy nights, in addition to outdoor patios in the front and back. A part of the pub is non-smoking. Very cozy with a highly authentic feel and friendly professional staff.

listings.name: Brutopia
listings.content: Brewpub with their own beers on tap on the busy Crescent strip. English-speaking college crowd.

listings.name: Peel Pub
listings.content: Montreal legend. Sports bar. Dirt cheap specials. Good time, particularly on $1 shooter Thursdays.

listings.name: Reggie's Bar
listings.content: Concordia University's bar. Features special Hockey nights, and cheap Thursday beer and shots. Great part of student-life experience.

listings.name: Le Vieux Dublin
listings.content: Don't let the Vieux Dublin sign outside fool you — this pub is not one bit Irish. There's not a lot of Emerald Island schlock around, but the pints are good, and home-style meals for lunch and dinner really hit the spot. There's live music on weekends on the minuscule stage, but during the week it's quiet and comfy. Staff is polite and nice.

listings.name: Time Supper Club
listings.content: The first Supper Club in the city, Time Supper Club starts as a restaurant and slowly turns into a night club.

listings.name: La Boom
listings.content: One of the trendiest clubs in Montreal. Be well-dressed and have a well-dressed wallet.

listings.name: Pang Pang Karaoke Bar
listings.content: Very comfy rooms in a range of sizes can be hired by the hour, from $30.

listings.name: K-Karaoke
listings.content: Large rooms with clean decoration.

listings.name: Abri du voyageur Hotel
listings.content: Charming hotel for budget-conscious travellers. Renovated historical building recommended by many guides as an excellent value with a personal touch.

listings.name: HI-Montréal
listings.content: Friendly and helpful staff. Activities organized every day (pub crawls, bike tours, urban walks, etc.) Dormitories and private rooms.

listings.name: University Bed & Breakfast
listings.content: Private rooms with shared bathroom and apartment suites with private bathroom, kitchenette and private entrance.

listings.name: Hotel Villa
listings.content: Continental breakfast.

listings.name: Le Centre Sheraton Montreal Hotel
listings.content: Offers 825 renovated rooms, free internet use in the Link@Sheraton lobby connectivity hub.

listings.name: Marriott Residence Inn Montreal Downtown
listings.content: With fully equipped kitchens and complimentary daily hot and cold buffet breakfast, Free WiFi access, rooftop terrace, laundry facility, friendly multi-lingual staff,

listings.name: Fairmont The Queen Elizabeth
listings.content: Offering 1,037 rooms, of which 100 are suites. Offers a health club, an indoor pool, and three restaurants: Les Voyageurs lounge, Le Montréalais bistro-restaurant and Beaver Club.

listings.name: Hotel Le Dauphin Montréal Centre-Ville
listings.content: Modern hotel with spacious rooms and a high level of service, within walking distance of the Old Town and modern city centre. Rooms are equipped with tea/coffee service, an Apple TV unit, and a computer. Rates include breakfast, newspapers, and wireless Internet access. Substantial discounts available for booking through the hotel’s web site.

listings.name: Hotel (10)
listings.content: A modern hotel with great design near boulevard Saint-Laurent.

listings.name: Hotel Le Germain Montreal
listings.content: A chic and intimate boutique-hotel designed for a hip clientele of leisure and business travelers.

listings.name: Loews Hotel Vogue
listings.content: Close to the corner of rue Sainte-Catherine.

listings.name: Le Meridien Versailles-Montreal
listings.content: This boutique hotel is in the chic Golden Square Mile neighborhood. This hotel features 108 rooms.

listings.name: Hyatt Regency Montreal
listings.content: Attached to the Complexe Desjardins.

listings.name: Hotel Omni Mont-Royal
listings.content: This five-star, four-diamond luxury hotel is centered amongst fashionable boutiques, museums, fine dining, and the exciting nightlife of Montreal's chic rue Crescent.

listings.name: Ritz-Carlton Montreal
listings.content: A historic luxury hotel, opened in 1912, that has played host to many famous figures such as Elizabeth Taylor, Winston Churchill and Queen Elizabeth II.

listings.name: Stade olympique
listings.content: Built for the 1976 Montreal Olympics, this amazing and controversial building's tower (from which the roof is suspended) is the world's tallest leaning structure. The roof, which could originally be raised, has been replaced numerous times and is the source of great local controversy. You can take a funicular to the top of the Olympic Tower for an incredible view of the city. Also has a public sports center that includes an Olympic-size swimming pool. The area around the stadium is a mecca for skateboarding, BMX-biking, and even snowboarding. the many slanted walls, hand rails and stairs give participants a concrete playground to entertain themselves.

listings.name: Insectarium
listings.content: The Insectarium is a museum centred on the insect world. A few living specimens and many displays, with occasional special exhibits, sometimes offering visitors the opportunity to eat various insect-based dishes from around the world.

listings.name: Jardin botanique de Montréal
listings.content: Huge and stunning botanical garden. Its themed gardens include a First Nations (Indigenous) garden, and Japanese, Chinese and Alpine gardens. Home to the annual Chinese lantern festival every autumn. During winter only the greenhouses are open to visitors.

listings.name: Biodôme
listings.content: The former Olympic Velodrome is now a showcase of different ecosystems.

listings.name: Planétarium Rio Tinto Alcan
listings.content: Exhibitions on space and astronomy.
listings.price: Free entrance to exhibits. Price for tickets to theatres: Adult $21.50, senior $19.25, student $15.50, child 5-17 $10.75, family $59

listings.name: Le Musée du Château Dufresne
listings.price: $8 adults, $7 students/seniors, $4.50 children 5-17, free children under 5

listings.name: CF Montréal
listings.content: Members of Major League Soccer since 2012, and one of three Canadian teams in the otherwise U.S.-based league. While not as widely followed as the Canadiens, CFM (originally the Montreal Impact) are still a major force in the city's sports scene, with routine sellouts of their stadium (which holds a shade under 21,000). Games for which an especially large crowd is expected are played at the Olympic Stadium—typically the home opener, and sometimes major in-season matchups or playoff games. As in several other sports, and in social and cultural matters, the Montreal–Toronto rivalry is present in soccer, with CFM matches against Toronto FC among the highlights of any season.

listings.name: Boutique Arhoma
listings.content: Specialized bakery and dairy. Coffee.

listings.name: Hoche Café
listings.content: Specialized coffee shop. Serves breakfast, lunch, drinks and coffee.

listings.name: Miami Deli
listings.content: Wide menu featuring French, Québécois, Italian, Greek and fast food dishes in a bistro setting with cute terrace in the summer.

listings.name: Bistro L'Adresse
listings.content: French bistro

listings.name: Sata Sushi
listings.content: Trendy sushi restaurant

listings.name: Café Atomic
listings.content: great espresso and delicious snacks in a retro setting

listings.name: Le Trèfle
listings.content: In an Irish Pub style, taste more than 100 of the finest beers, renowned scotch and a varied and quality bistro menu

listings.name: Hotel Universel Montreal
listings.content: Located within a 5-minute walk of Olympic Stadium, 10-minute walk of Montreal Biodome botanical garden, and 5 km of downtown Montreal. Hotel offers a full-service spa, indoor pool, seasonal outdoor pool, sauna, gym, jacuzzi, free parking, and bicycle rack. Complimentary shuttle service is available to Viau metro station. Rooms are equipped with a fridge, coffee maker, and cable TV. Some rooms feature views of Olympic Stadium.

listings.name: Maison Montplaisir
listings.content: Bed & breakfast.

listings.name: Church of St. Michael and St. Anthony
listings.image: Church of St. Michael and St. Anthony.jpg

listings.name: St-Viateur Bagel
listings.content: The flagship bakery of St-Viateur Bagel. Cash only. No longer 24/7 after the COVID-19 pandemic.

listings.name: Latina
listings.content: Fine food shops boasting an excellent olive bar and many European importations. It is one of the rare places to buy truffles in Montreal.

listings.name: Le Cagibi
listings.content: A nice vegetarian café and bistro, Le Cagibi is also a hot spot of the emerging experimental music scene with live shows most nights of the week.

listings.name: La Poule
listings.content: One of the best Portuguese-style chicken restaurants in the entire city (and there are quite a few.) It's owned by an Italian woman and the head chef is a Moroccan man, but no matter. Their chicken is grilled, not rotisserie. Served with piri-piri hot sauce, choice of salads and a huge pile of fresh fries. Lots of other things on the menu but don't bother. It's all about la poule (the chicken).

listings.name: Arahova
listings.content: A Greek restaurant specialized souvlaki and doner. A chain, and not a great one at that.

listings.name: Plus que Parfait
listings.content: Gelato

listings.name: Café Olympico
listings.content: Coffee shop.

listings.name: Café Club Social
listings.content: Coffee shop.

listings.name: B&M
listings.content: A restaurant with questionable service. Known for good North American style pizza. Brunches are only fair.

listings.name: Comptoir 21
listings.content: Awesome fish and chips.

listings.name: Helm brasseur gourmand
listings.content: A unique bar with emphasis on local products including homemade beers, ciders, and North American wines. On the food side, you will find tapas like platters prepared with fresh ingredients: fish and meat tartares, duck magret, Québec cheeses, rillete, foie-gras, the famous veal mini-burgers, and also vegetable dishes. Food is not necessarily of the quality one would expect for the price, however.
listings.price: $4 draft beer ($5.50 for pint), 5 to 8 prices on tap

listings.name: Sault-au-Récollet
listings.content: One of the oldest villages on the island of Montreal, it retains its village atmosphere with many houses dating from the 18th and 19th centuries. It was the original site of Fort Lorette, a trading post and mission for the conversion of the First Nations people of the area.

listings.name: Cité des arts du cirque, TOHU
listings.content: A centre for performance, creativity, experimentation, and convergence of culture, the environment and community involvement.

listings.name: Orioles de Montréal baseball team
listings.content: Ligue de Baseball Élite du Québec team.
listings.address: Gary Carter Stadium (formerly Marcel-Clement Field) in Ahuntsic Park

listings.name: Chez Benny Express
listings.content: Kosher fast-food restaurant with Mediterranean grilled meats.

listings.name: Famous Pizza
listings.content: Kosher pizzeria.

listings.name: Restaurant Le St-Urbain
listings.content: Modern cuisine made from products of the market, often organic, and from the Quebec terroir. The menu varies with the seasons. Tasting menu and the food-wine pairings. Many of the dishes use vacuum cooking techniques and their in-house smokehouse.

listings.name: La bella Italiana
listings.content: Wood oven pizza, pastas, gelato, Italian coffee.

listings.name: Bar Pam Pam
listings.content: A dive bar enjoyed for its cheap beer and pool tables.

listings.name: Bar Le Grand Chapeau
listings.content: Sports bar, billards, cocktails, Happy Hour 17:00-19:00.

listings.name: Gite du Grenier
listings.content: B&B. 20-min walk to the metro. Free parking.

listings.name: Le Gite de l'ecole
listings.content: B&B. 5-min walk to Metro Jarry. Free parking.

listings.name: Vieux-Port
listings.content: The Old Port is a large waterfront green space with attractions such as Cirque du Soleil, the Montreal Science Center, the Labyrinth, the Clock Tower, and a large outdoor audio-visual stage which is the site for the Canada Day fireworks.
listings.address: South of rue Saint-Antoine between rue McGill and rue Berri

listings.name: Place Jacques-Cartier
listings.content: Pedestrian street filled with street artists and musicians, and there are numerous fine restaurants and private art galleries nearby.

listings.name: Notre-Dame Basilica
listings.content: Probably the city's most spectacular church, a gem of Victorian Gothic. Service is at 17:00 daily and on Sunday morning. Entrance is free for worship, but donations are suggested. During service, the organ music is not to be missed. While it shouldn't have to be mentioned, tourists should be respectful during services. Photography is not allowed during services. 20-minute guided tours offered in French or English.
listings.price: Adults $14, student (17-22) children (6-16) $9, children under 6 free

listings.name: Montreal Clock Tower
listings.content: Also known as the Sailors' Memorial Clock, the clock tower was built between 1919-1922 as a memorial to sailors lost at sea. Its clock mechanism is similar to Big Ben's and was known for its accuracy; sailors would often set their watches by it. The clock tower is no longer open to visitors.
listings.image: Montreal Clock Tower and Jacques Cartier Bridge01.JPG

listings.name: Former Parliament in Montreal
listings.content: While Montreal was the capital of Canada from 1843 to 1849, it also hosted the parliament building. The building was burnt to the ground by rioters in 1849. Some of the artifacts uncovered from the site are displayed in a self-guided tour.

listings.name: Pointe-à-Callière Museum
listings.content: A modern museum built over the ruins of Montreal's first settlement, Pointe à Callière. This museum uses audiovisual technology as well as surrounding archaeological remains to tell the story of Montreal from the first natives to the present day.

listings.name: Sir George-Étienne Cartier National Historic Site
listings.content: Reconstruction of two 19th-century Victorian homes commemorating the life and accomplishments of Sir George-Étienne Cartier, who was a Canadian statesman and Father of Confederation.
listings.price: $4.25/adult, $3.75/senior, youth free, $3.75 per person in commercial group

listings.name: Montréal Science Centre
listings.content: Interactive science museum and IMAX theater.
listings.price: IMAX screenings $8.50 child, $10.50 teen, $11.50 adult, $10.50 senior; exhibitions $8.50 child, $13 teen, $15 adult, $13 senior, $40 family; see website for details

listings.name: Centre d'histoire de Montréal
listings.content: Covering the history of Montreal from its founding in 1535. The museum is housed in a former fire station that dates from 1903.
listings.price: $6 adults, $5 seniors, $4 children (6-17) and students, $15 families, free for children under 6

listings.name: Bank of Montréal Museum
listings.content: Hands-on museum focusing on the history of banking in Montreal.

listings.name: Château Ramezay Museum
listings.content: 18th century Governor's residence and gardens full of historical artifacts from daily life.

listings.name: DHC/ART
listings.content: A privately endowed foundation, DHC/ART is a permanent location for exciting and relevant temporary visual arts exhibitions and projects.

listings.name: Winter Ice Skating
listings.price: $4 adults, $3 child (does not include skate rental)

listings.name: Voiles en voiles
listings.content: This venue offers a diverse range of outdoor activities, including aerial adventure courses, wall climbing, and inflatable games, all set within a thematic environment inspired by 18th-century pirate and royal ships.

listings.name: Olive & Gourmando
listings.content: Popular boulangerie offering fresh sandwiches, soups, and a daily lunch dish and baked goods. Also sells breads, jams, and snacks to take away.

listings.name: Marché du Vieux
listings.content: Equal parts bistro and fine-food boutique, Marché du Vieux is a cute spot for a gourmet lunch or snack.

listings.name: Le Jardin Nelson
listings.content: Fancy and filling crepes are the main draw to this historic restaurant and garden courtyard. Offering outdoor jazz and other live music in the summer, it loses some of its charm in the winter when things move inside.

listings.name: Boris Bistro
listings.content: Popular bistro featuring a large courtyard. Menu offers meats, seafood, and pastas. Try the French fries cooked in duck fat.

listings.name: Restaurant Le Fripon
listings.content: Grand historic building with shaded terrace serving French bistro fare, seafood, and pastas. Note the terrace menu is limited to soups, snails, and fries. Bar features wide selection of domestic and imported beers.

listings.name: Chez Suzette
listings.content: Crepes and fondue in a cozy, family-friendly spot. Wine and cider at SAQ prices + $5.

listings.name: Sushi-ya
listings.content: Well-executed and beautifully presented sushi and tempura in an elegant dining room. Staff speaks English as well as French.

listings.name: Gibby's
listings.content: Fancy steakhouse housed in a 200-year-old former stable, popular with tourists. Reservations strongly recommended.

listings.name: Le Saint-Gabriel
listings.content: French fine cuisine with a taste of Quebec from the first North America alcohol licence, issued in 1754.

listings.name: Kyo Bar Japonais
listings.content: Upscale Japanese restaurant and sushi bar with a menu based on izakaya classics and an extensive sake selection.

listings.name: Toqué!
listings.content: In 1993, chef Normand Laprise put Montreal cuisine on the map with this landmark restaurant, and after more than 25 years, it's still going strong in a new location. Combining the latest trends in fine dining with local and regional produce, the chefs create spectacularly complex dishes in tiny, but strangely satisfying portions. The house specialty is an eight-course surprise menu, made up of many small dishes. This restaurant will take a bite out of your wallet, but serious foodies will find it worth the cost.

listings.name: Pub St-Paul
listings.content: Big space, popular with tours. Offers pub grub and a view of the river during the day and live music (Th-Sa 22:00). Cheap (for Old Montreal) and casual.

listings.name: Santos
listings.content: Cafe-by-day and bar-by-night, Santos is the place to escape your hotel lobby for a martini and late night snack of "Pop Food", their take on tapas. Live jazz on Thursdays, DJ on the weekends. Reservations recommended for Saturday nights. Weekend covers start around $20.

listings.name: Wunderbar
listings.content: Trendy spot on the edge of Old Montreal. Expect cover charges and a line at the door. Changing out of your sight-seeing clothes and into something swanky will probably help get you in the door.

listings.name: Suite 701
listings.content: "Suite" sums it up for this high-end lounge popular with the executive set. Leather couches and sipping scotches.

listings.name: Alternative Hostel of Old Montreal
listings.content: Housed in a 19th-century warehouse, this hostel boasts fair trade coffee, wi-fi, an organic continental breakfast, and a range of activities and classes. Kitchen and laundry facilities provided. Often full, reservations recommended.

listings.name: Auberge Vieux Port
listings.content: A good deal for the price, this historical building, set back from the street, books up early.

listings.name: Le Westin Montreal
listings.content: 454 large and well-appointed guestrooms at the gateway to Old Montreal. Each room features the ten-layer Heavenly Bed, and the hotel also offers a unique glass-bottom pool.

listings.name: Hotel Epik Montreal
listings.content: Three-star boutique hotel.

listings.name: Trylon Hotels
listings.content: A modern, renovated hotel. Rooftop terrace, lounge, indoor pool. 2 min from the entertainment district & grocery store.

listings.name: Hotel St-Paul
listings.content: This self-described "design hotel" in Old Montreal features uber-modern rooms on the edge of the historical district. See Eat and Drink for bars and restaurants in the same building.

listings.name: Hotel Nelligan
listings.content: Falling somewhere between posh and opulent, the Nelligan offers large rooms with king beds, loft-style suites, and rooftop two-room penthouses above a fine French restaurant. Some rooms with fireplaces, and jacuzzi-tubs for two.

listings.name: Hotel Gault
listings.content: Feels like you're stepping into Architectural Digest with ultra-modern furniture and rooms in a converted warehouse. Very helpful staff.

listings.name: Le Saint Sulpice
listings.content: Four-star boutique hotel offering four types of luxury suites.

listings.name: Le Petit Hotel
listings.content: A boutique hotel, Le Petit Hotel is charming, chic and hip in the middle of Old Montreal. It combines 19th-century architecture with 21st century tech such as Wi-Fi, iPod docking station, LCDs, Nintendo Wii and multi-jet showers.

listings.name: W Montreal
listings.content: A luxury hotel, the W Montreal has 152 rooms, spa, and a restaurant - Otto Ristorante. This hotel is between downtown and Old Montreal.

listings.name: Beaubien Monument
listings.content: Located in Parc Beaubien.

listings.name: Café Souvenir
listings.content: 24 hour cafe with basic eats.

listings.name: Le Glacier Bilboquet
listings.content: Ben and Jerry's-style ice cream - sweet, with chunky bits. Delicious sorbets too. A very popular place in the summer, it is not unusual to see lengthy queues outside the shop.

listings.name: Mamie Clafoutis
listings.content: Popular bakery known for their baguettes.

listings.name: Bruno Bistro
listings.content: Friendly neighbourhood French bistro.

listings.name: Breakfast à Montreal
listings.content: Two simple rooms in an apartment. Organic continental breakfast.

listings.name: Cite Chic Couette
listings.content: Three rooms in a 1908 building furnished with antiques. Private garden. Continental breakfast.

listings.name: Montreal Biosphère
listings.content: The former United States pavilion from Expo 67, a geodesic dome designed by R. Buckminster Fuller. It now houses an Environment Canada museum dedicated to water and the environment.

listings.name: Habitat 67
listings.content: This visually striking residential building was created by architect Moshe Safdie for Expo 67. The result was an amazingly modern dwelling that challenged the way architects created urban homes. Compared alternately to a beehive, a Taos pueblo, and a crystalline growth, the complex's 154 units are composed of prefabricated concrete cubes assembled on site. The apartments here are highly prized and a number of prominent Montrealers make Habitat 67 their home.

listings.name: Formula 1 Grand Prix
listings.content: The Canadian Grand Prix or Formula One is a must-see for any petrolhead or sports fan. It attracts up to 100,000 people and spans a weekend, with practice and qualifying on Friday and Saturday and the race on Sunday. Wheelchair-accessible seats are available. The next most recent F1 is 21-23 May 2027.

listings.name: Montreal Casino
listings.content: Opened in 1993, this is the largest casino in Canada. Open to visitors aged 18 or older.

listings.name: Osheaga Music and Arts Festival
listings.content: A three-day indie & alternative rock festival held annually in Parc Jean-Drapeau on Île Sainte-Hélène at the end of July/beginning of August.

listings.name: Beach park
listings.content: Clean water and sand attracts families to this small, man-made beach at the south tip of Ile Notre Dame. Activities include a playground, volleyball, and watercraft rentals. There are bathrooms, changing rooms, and a snack bar.
listings.price: Ages 14 and up $8, 6-13 $4, 65+ $7, family $20. Season passes available

listings.name: Île Notre-Dame lake and at the Olympic Basin.
La Ronde
listings.content: An amusement park that is a member of the Six Flags chain.
listings.price: Discounts are readily available: a Coca-Cola tin is worth an $8 discount on any rides ticket

listings.name: Snack Bar Espace-Bouffe
listings.content: Basic chips-and-hot-dog snack bar.

listings.name: La Bonne Carte
listings.content: Lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch are offered at the Casino buffet.

listings.name: Nuances
listings.content: French haute cuisine with a Quebec edge served far removed from the noise of the casino. Choose between lobster, Quebec lamb, loin of deer, and other season specialties or try the chefs "discovery menu". Note, no exceptions are made to the Casinos: strict 18 & up policy.

listings.name: Festin du Gouverneur
listings.content: Set menu (meat, fish, and veggie options) with historical reenactment show.

listings.name: Vieux-Moulin de Pointe-aux-Trembles
listings.content: On the banks of the St. Lawrence River, the Old Mill is a witness of the seigneurial regime in New France. Built around 1720, this mill is one of the oldest and highest in Quebec. The history is explained through multimedia tools and fun animations.
listings.address: Parc du Vieux-Moulin, 11630 rue Notre-Dame Est (at 2nd Avenue)

listings.name: Public art: The Sculpted Trees of Bout-de-l'Île
listings.content: As part of the project, the borough produced sculptures from diseased trees that had to be felled. Two artists created seven works in three borough parks: Bout-de-l'Île Park, Moulin-du-Rapide Park and Pierre-Dagenais-dit-Lépine-dit-Lépine Park.

listings.name: Island of Poets
listings.content: The Île aux poètes trail project aims to make poetry more accessible to the general public. In Rivière-des-Prairies-Pointe-aux-Trembles, Poets Island will take the form of benches set up in the borough's parks. These stone-filled banks from the banks of the St. Lawrence River, the Rivière des Prairies and Saint-Venant-de-Paquette are in symbiosis with nature and are places of contemplation. Plaques will be installed nearby, on which will be engraved poems of Montreal artists, from yesterday to today, in French and other languages.

listings.name: Club de Golf Metropolitain Anjou
listings.content: Two 18-hole golf courses. “Aux Quatre Vents” restaurant open year-round.

listings.name: Tomate Basilic
listings.content: Italian.

listings.name: Grillades Sizzle
listings.content: Portuguese grill.

listings.name: Burger de Ville
listings.content: 100% Canadian beef, always fresh, never frozen. Steak is graded AAA, and properly aged.

listings.name: Quality Hotel Montreal East
listings.content: Fitness centre, Italian restaurant, pets accepted for a fee, free Wi-Fi. Near Galleries dAnjou shopping centre.

listings.name: Motel Le Paysan
listings.content: 2-star hotel. Pet-friendly accommodation. Free WiFi is offered throughout the property and free private parking is available on site. Every room includes a TV and a private bathroom fitted with a bath or shower. 24-hour front desk.
